ai.description: This 4–6 cm frog is brown with darker dorsal mottling and a pale belly. It features a distinct dark mask, prominent skin warts, and a robust head with a rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes khasianus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored tympanum, which is noticeably smaller than the eye in this species.
ai.habitat: *Limnonectes khasianus* inhabits moist, evergreen hill forests and rocky stream banks within the Indian subcontinent, typically at altitudes between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Khasi Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky banks of mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Khasi Wart Frog breeds in streams during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of pigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Khasi Wart Frog occurs in Northeast India, specifically across the states of Meghalaya, Assam, and Nagaland, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Khasi Wart Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard near small, rocky forest streams.
